objective: Map how HolyAgent bundles and uses its vendored ripgrep and fd executables, to plan replacing the bundling with declared dependencies.
scope: Read in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-deps (clean tree at the 0.3.2 browser-use head). The maintainer's ask: "remove the bundling of the executables, list them as dependencies instead".

Answer with file:line: 1. Where the vendored binaries live (paths, which platforms and archs, sizes if visible), how they are pinned and checksummed (scripts/update-dependencies.ts, scripts/dependency-pins.ts, any pin file), how the build puts them into packages/integrations/claude/dist and packages/integrations/pi/dist, and whether git carries the binaries or the build downloads them. 2. Every runtime consumer: `holyagent rg` / `holyagent fd` CLI commands, the Pi tools (fff, search, bash), hooks, setup or doctor, and how each finds the binary (bundled path, PATH fallback?). 3. Every place text promises the bundled binaries: root instructions (requirements tree and generated agent files such as packages/integrations/claude/dist/agents/holyagent.md, which says the CLI runs 'the ripgrep and fd that ship with the plugin, so every machine gives the same answer'), docs (docs/development.md, install docs, README), AGENTS.md, CI workflows, tests (scripts/*.test.ts). 4. How each install path gets dependencies today: the Claude Code plugin (synced files, any install step?), the Pi package (npm dependencies installed by pi install?), mise.toml tools for development, and setup/doctor's existing 'needs' mechanism (uvx, npx, chromium). 5. Whether npm packages already exist in the dependency tree that ship rg or fd (e.g. @vscode/ripgrep, fd-find), and whether fff (@ff-labs/pi-fff) needs its own binary.
constraints: Read only; make no edits and no git writes.
Report in under 500 words, with file:line for each claim.

criteria.text: Each of the five questions is answered with file:line evidence or marked not found

result:
result: ripgrep and fd are vendored only in the Claude plugin, and git commits the binaries. All five questions are answered below. I had no shell, so I could not run `git ls-files` or measure sizes; the "committed" claim rests on docs (docs/development.md:153, docs/decisions.md:53).

Q1. Where the binaries live and how they are pinned (all paths under /home/user/holyagent-0.3.2-deps)
- Files: `packages/integrations/claude/dist/scripts/vendor/{darwin-arm64,linux-x64}/{rg,fd}` and `windows-x64/{rg,fd}.exe`, each with `licenses/<project>/` (Glob result). `VENDOR_DIRECTORY` is defined at `packages/integrations/claude/src/files.ts:25`.
- Size: "about 24 MB" is the documented figure (docs/decisions.md:53). I did not measure it.
- The pin file is `packages/integrations/claude/src/vendor.ts`.
  - It holds `RIPGREP_VERSION` and `FD_VERSION` (ripgrep 15.2.0 per the doc comment at line 30).
  - `ASSETS` (line 94) lists 3 targets per tool: darwin-arm64, linux-x64 (musl) and windows-x64. Each pin has a GitHub release URL (line 63), an archive SHA-256 and a binary SHA-256.
  - `vendorProblems` is at line 159; `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES` (64 MiB) is at line 181.
- Download and verify: `scripts/vendor.ts:97-111` downloads only what is missing or wrong, then runs `removeUnpinned`. The download has a 60 s timeout and the 64 MiB cap (lines 20-44).
- Updater: `scripts/update-dependencies.ts`.
  - Remotes are at lines 181-182: ripgrep takes its hash from a `.sha256` file, fd from the GitHub API `digest`.
  - `VENDOR_PINS` is at line 191, the survey at 384, the rewrite at 788-813, and it ends by running `bun scripts/vendor.ts`.
  - The pure rewrite helpers (`VendoredTool`, `rewriteVendoredTool`) are in `scripts/dependency-pins.ts:265-309`.
- Build wiring: `mise.toml:57-64`. The `vendor` task runs `bun scripts/vendor.ts`, and `build` depends on `vendor`. `packages/integrations/claude/build.ts:24-31` clears the generated paths but excludes `VENDOR_DIRECTORY`.
- Git carries the binaries: docs/development.md:153 says "The vendor folder is committed, because the marketplace serves the plugin from `dist/`".
- Pi: `packages/integrations/pi/dist` has no vendor folder (Glob found only the claude one), and `packages/integrations/pi/src` has no vendor references.

Q2. Runtime consumers and how each finds the binary
- The only consumers I found are the `holyagent rg` and `holyagent fd` CLI commands, in `packages/runtime/src/cli/tools.ts`.
  - The folder is `BUNDLED_TOOLS = join(import.meta.dir,"vendor")` (line 38), passed as `tools: host.tools ?? BUNDLED_TOOLS` (`packages/runtime/src/cli/program.ts:84`).
  - `TARGETS` (lines 28-32) holds the three platforms. `selectTarget` fails with `UnsupportedPlatform` (line 68); `runTool` fails with `ToolMissing` (lines 90-91) when `<dir>/<target>/<tool>` is absent.
  - It runs the binary with the Bun `$` shell (line 93) and returns the exit code.
  - There is no PATH fallback.
- Agents are told to fall back to system rg/fd themselves on `UnsupportedPlatform` (requirements/root/search.md:1, specialist/working.md:2).
- I found no use of the binaries in hooks, setup or doctor, in the Pi tools (fff, bash), or in `packages/runtime/src/pi/fff/settings.ts:34` beyond a comment.
- Pi bash is `just-bash` (`dist/scripts/just-bash.js`); I did not trace whether it calls rg.
- Hypothesis: in Pi, `holyagent rg` fails with `ToolMissing`, because the Pi `dist/scripts/holyagent.js:28676` computes the same vendor path and no vendor folder exists. Unverified; I did not run it. If true, the Pi root's search rule is already broken.
- Errors: `packages/runtime/src/cli/errors.ts:128-131`. `ToolMissing` tells the user to run `mise run vendor`.

Q3. Text and tests that promise the bundled binaries
- Instructions: `requirements/root/search.md:1`, `requirements/specialist/working.md:2`, and the per-model copies under `kimi-k3.1/`, `gpt-6/` and `claude-5.5/` (`root/search.md` and `specialist/working.md`).
- Coverage: `packages/runtime/src/instructions/coverage.ts:71`, `:180`, `:395` and `:697`. The line 180 phrase "Search with the ripgrep and fd that ship with the plugin" must appear in the generated text.
- Generated files: `packages/integrations/claude/dist/agents/holyagent.md:100`, the Pi `dist/agents/*.md` and `dist/families/*/agents/*.md`, and the bundles `dist/scripts/holyagent.js` and `dist/extensions/holyagent.js`.
- Agent tool selection: `packages/integrations/claude/src/agents.ts:81` and `:261` (roles with Bash get no Grep or Glob).
- `cli/tools.ts:99-138` (summaries and notes) and `docs/pi/search.md:3` ("The Claude plugin keeps the bundled ripgrep and fd").
- Docs:
  - `docs/components.md:19` and `:47-49`
  - `docs/decisions.md:53`
  - `docs/development.md:12`, `:68`, `:94`, `:100`, `:153`
  - `docs/attributions.md:14-15` (licenses travel in `dist/scripts/vendor/...`)
  - `AGENTS.md:43` ("vendored ripgrep and fd")
  - `README.md:52` (credits only)
  - `docs/pi/claude-parity.md:90`
- CI workflows: no matches in `.github/workflows/*.yml` for vendor or `.exe`.
- Tests: `scripts/vendor.test.ts`, `scripts/dependency-pins.test.ts:212-265`, `scripts/update-dependencies.test.ts:203-280`, `packages/integrations/claude/tests/vendor.test.ts:47-55` (offline pin check and executable bit), `packages/integrations/claude/tests/plugin.test.ts:109-119` and `:183-190`, and `packages/runtime/tests/tools.test.ts:79` and `:96-101`.

Q4. How each install path gets dependencies
- Claude plugin: it ships the committed `dist/`, so it has no install step and the binaries arrive as synced files.
- Pi package: pinned npm packages in `packages/runtime/src/config/pi-packages.json:10` (`"@ff-labs/pi-fff": "0.11.0"`) are installed by setup. The Pi `dist` carries no rg or fd.
- mise.toml `[tools]` (lines 1-8) lists only node and bun, so development has no rg or fd tool. The vendor task fills the plugin instead.
- The `needs` mechanism is `SystemNeed` in `packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts:58-78`, with kinds `display`, `command`, `chromium` and `node`.
  - `kind:"command"` with `command: "uvx"` is used at lines 507-508, and `npx` at line 269.
  - `pi-check.ts:371-383` checks it: "needs ${command} on PATH; ${fix}". `capabilities.ts:429` shows `health` includes `"needs"`.
  - It is per Pi capability only. The Claude path has no equivalent: doctor.ts and setup contain no rg or fd check (grep found none).
  - A `command` need for rg and fd would reuse this. I did not read the exact fields of the `command` shape.

Q5. Existing npm packages
- `bun.lock` has no match for `@vscode/ripgrep`, `fd-find`, `ripgrep` or `@ff-labs`. No npm package in the tree ships rg or fd.
- fff: docs/pi/search.md:3 and :15 say it is an in-process Rust binding with "no `fd` or `rg` process per call" and "needs nothing of the system". `@ff-labs/fff-node` ships its own native library for darwin, linux, win32 and android (docs/pi/search.md:11). It is the Pi-side search and is independent of rg and fd.

notes:
- Removing the bundling touches the `UnsupportedPlatform`/`ToolMissing` semantics, the coverage phrase at coverage.ts:180, every generated agent file, AGENTS.md:43, and the update-dependencies vendor path (the vendor pins and the `scripts/vendor.ts` hook are all deleted).
- Replacing the pins means choosing a new source: a PATH requirement checked by a doctor need, or an npm package.

evidence:
Each of the five questions is answered with file:line evidence or marked not found: Q1 is at the paths above (`vendor.ts`, `scripts/vendor.ts`, `mise.toml:57-64`, `docs/development.md:153`). Q2 is at `cli/tools.ts` and `program.ts:84`. Q3 is the list of instruction, doc and test lines above. Q4 is at `mise.toml:1-8`, `capabilities.ts:58-78` and `pi-check.ts:371-383`. Q5 is the `bun.lock` grep (no match) and docs/pi/search.md:3,11,15.
findings: the report above. Not verified: the git tracking itself, binary sizes, and the Pi `ToolMissing` behavior at runtime.
